title: BioArctic left out in the cold as Novartis walks away from $800M neuro collab
summary: Just 14 months after Novartis signed an $800 million biobucks neuroscience partnership with BioArctic, the Swiss pharma has walked away from the deal.

title: FDA grants uniQure’s Huntington’s gene therapy priority review, teeing up ‘defining milestone’
summary: The FDA has accepted uniQure’s priority review and application for its gene therapy treatment for Huntington’s disease.

title: Karyopharm files Chapter 11, lines up Ayrmid as lead bidder in planned merger
summary: In an answer to Karyopharm's cash crisis, Irish biotech Ayrmid has agreed to make the first bid on the struggling biopharma's assets in a court supervised auction, teeing up a potential hematology merger.

title: OpenAI-funded Biossil snags Theriva's unwanted antibiotic degrader portfolio for up to $91M
summary: Canada's OpenAI-backed startup Biossil Labs has extended its pharma shopping spree with a deal worth up to $91 million for Theriva Biologics' deprioritized early- to mid-stage portfolio of antibiotic-degrading enzymes.

title: Teva ends trial of one of its original line-up of innovative meds over futility
summary: Teva has given up on a key trial of one of its original line-up of innovative medicines.

title: FDA dims Bright Minds’ outlook with partial hold on seizure trial over toxicity in mice
summary: The FDA has put a partial hold on Bright Minds Biosciences’ seizure study application over preclinical toxicity data and concerns about its preparations for enrolling children.

title: Lower dose of Tiziana's MS drug reduces neuroinflammation, while higher dose struggles
summary: Tiziana Life Sciences’ intranasal drug has hit the dual endpoints of a phase 2a study in patients with a form of multiple sclerosis (MS), although the win was slightly marred by the higher dose missing a key neuroinflammation goal.

title: The cost of waiting: What reaching clinical proof-of-concept sooner means for biotech cash burn
summary: Explore how delays before clinical proof-of-concept increase biotech cash burn, and how connected drug development can preserve capital and runway.

title: China's InventisBio delivers competitive TYK2 data in phase 3 psoriasis win
summary: A phase 3 trial of InventisBio’s nomelcitinib has hit its primary endpoint, delivering evidence that the TYK2 inhibitor can hold its own against rival psoriasis drugs.

title: Gilead reveals partial clinical hold on 2 CAR-T cell therapy trials
summary: Gilead Sciences announced on its third-quarter earnings call Oct. 29 that the company has placed a partial clinical hold on two studies for the CAR-T cell therapy KITE-753 in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL).

title: When drug development gets personal
summary: When Third Rock Ventures partner Jigar Raythatha was diagnosed with brain cancer, he found himself relying on a drug originally developed by Agios, a biotech his firm backed years before he joined. On "The Top Line," he shares how the experience changed his perspective on drug development.

title: Chutes & Ladders—Lilly unifies global markets as 36-year vet Patrik Jonsson retires
summary: Lilly will unite its U.S. and international commercial units as a long-time exec retires. Enanta's CEO will hang up his hat after 23 year at the helm. Estrella has tapped a new a CEO to lead it through a clinical trial.

title: Bracco invests $230M in first US diagnostic imaging manufacturing facility

title: Jazz's $820M Actio buyout gives rise to Setara, armed with $90M series A

title: AstraZeneca cuts early-phase prostate cancer pipeline

title: Bambusa shoots past IPO targets as Aspen trims offering
summary: Bambusa Therapeutics has upsized its IPO, selling more shares at the midpoint of its target range to gross $168.9 million for bispecific R&D. But Aspen Neuroscience underperformed expectations, hitting the bottom end of its target range and selling slightly fewer shares than expected.
